paragraphs.text: Forbid foreground waiting in DSH agents: sleep / wait_agent / job_output(wait) are rejected with a b
ackground-job retry. 禁止 Agent 前台等待，会话不再被冻住。
# sleep-not-permitted
中文 · English

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that forbids
**foreground waiting**. When an agent tries to run a co

mmand whose purpose is waiting
(`sleep`, `wait`, `tail -f`, `watch`, `ping` without `-c`, infinite l

oops), or calls a blocking
wait tool (`wait_agent`, `job_output` with `wait: true`), the call is rej

ected — and the rejection
is a set of instructions: run it in the background (`run_in_background: tr

ue`), or end the turn and
let the completion notice wake you.

Nothing is silently rewritten: DSH logs and shows tool arguments before dispatch, so a guard can
onl
y refuse, not impersonate a different call. The plugin refuses, explains, and gets out of the way.
## Why a plugin, and not AGENTS.md or a preset

- **AGENTS.md is per-workspace.** You would have to write the rule into every workspace, and every
n

ew workspace silently misses it.
- **A preset is per-agent configuration.** Every composition needs

its own copy, and the user has to
pick it.
- **A host plugin is profile-level.** Install once and ev

ery workspace, session, and subagent is
covered. It can carry configuration, be upgraded, disabled,

e, session, and subagent is
covered. It can carry configuration, be upgraded, disabled, and removed.
## Why it is needed
A DSH session moves one step at a time: however long a foreground tool call runs, the session stops

with it. `bash({ command: "sleep 60" })` looks harmless but freezes the conversation for a minute,
a

nd a five-minute `wait_agent` freezes it for five. DSH has a safety net for slow *work* (a
foregroun

d command that exceeds its timeout is promoted to a background job), but that still burns
the timeou
t first — and waiting is not work at all.
So the plugin does two things:

1. **Prevention** — a rule in the system prompt, next to the existing background-jobs section, so
th

e model picks the background form first;
2. **Enforcement** — a synchronous `ctx.tools.guard()` deni

al when the foreground form is used
anyway, with the retry spelled out.
## What gets blocked

- **Waiting commands** in `bash` / `pwsh` / `terminal_send`: `sleep`, `wait`, `tail -f`, `watch`,
`p

ing` without `-c`, `yes`, infinite loops, log-follow modes — see the rule table below.
- **Blocking

wait tools**: `wait_agent` and `job_output` with `wait: true`, when the requested wait
exceeds the b

udget (default **30 seconds**).
- **Polling**: running the same check command more than `pollRepeatT

hreshold` times within
`pollWindowMs` — the "wait a little, check, wait a little, check" substitute

for sleeping. It is
refused with the same instruction: wrap the waiting itself in a background job.

- **Commands that need human input or confirmation**: `sudo` without `-n`, `ssh` without
`-o BatchMo

de=yes`, login/key-generation flows (`npm login`, `gh auth login`, `ssh-keygen`, …),
interactive edi

tors and pagers (`vim`, `less`, `top`, …), `docker run/exec -it`, `read -p`,
`rm/cp/mv -i`. They are

refused in the foreground *and* in the background: a background job has
no stdin, so it would hang
silently — never settling, never notifying.

If what you are waiting for has no DSH job handle (a remote host, an external service), be it a
comm

and or a poll: wrap the waiting itself in a background job — for example
`ssh host 'until [ -f done

]; do sleep 5; done'` with `run_in_background: true` (sleep is allowed
inside a background job) — th

en end the turn; that job's completion wakes the agent. This is the
correct replacement for both `sl
eep` and polling when there is nothing local to await.
## Behavior

- A foreground wait is rejected with `Error: <reason>`; the reason contains the exact retry form.
-

A call that already has `run_in_background: true` passes — that is the shape this plugin wants.
- Or

dinary commands (`git status`, `npm test`, `curl`, `grep`, …) pass untouched.
- `ask_user_question`

is not a wait — it is you being asked — and is never blocked.
- Non-blocking reads (`job_output` wit
hout `wait`, `list_agents`, `team_task_list`) pass.
The default budget (**30 s**) exists so short coordination waits keep working out of the box (DSH's
own Agent Teams guidance has the Lead wait for teammates). Waits above the budget — the five-minute

`wait_agent(timeout_ms: 300000)` case — are rejected. Set `maxBlockingWaitMs: 0` for strict mode:
no
t a single second of foreground waiting.
## After a background job finishes

A completion notice means the job **finished**, not that it succeeded. The notice carries the
status

(`completed` / `failed` / `killed`) plus the label; read the output and exit code with
`job_output`
before continuing, and diagnose a `failed`/`killed` job instead of retrying blindly.
Background jobs have **no timeout of their own**. A job that dies mid-flight or hangs while waiting
for something that never happens never settles — and so never notifies. Bound it yourself: wrap the

command in `timeout N`, keep a deadline in retry loops, or write a marker/report file at the end.
Fo

r cross-machine waits the same applies to the remote wait loop: give it a maximum wait and let it
ex
it with a failure marker on timeout, so the local job always settles and always notifies.

If the work needs a human decision in the middle, do not background it: confirm first
(`ask_user_que
stion`, or the DSH approval channel), then start it with non-interactive flags.
## Rules
| id | matches |
| `sleep` | `sleep N` in command position (`sudo sleep`, `timeout 30 sleep`, `do sleep`, `&& sleep`,

…) |
| `sleep-nested-shell` | nested shell payloads such as `bash -c "sleep 10"` |
| `sleep-script`

| `time.sleep(30)`, `python -c "...sleep(5)"` |
| `wait` | the shell builtin `wait` |
| `tail-follo

w` | `tail -f` / `tail -F` / `tail --follow` |
| `watch` | `watch <cmd>` (re-runs forever) |
| `ping

-forever` | `ping` without `-c` |
| `yes` | bare `yes` (endless output) |
| `infinite-loop` | `while

true` / `while :` / `until false` |
| `follow-logs` | `docker/podman logs -f`, `journalctl -f`, `ku

:` / `until false` |
| `follow-logs` | `docker/podman logs -f`, `journalctl -f`, `kubectl logs -f` |
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility

Tested against DSH `0.1.5-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.3`. It relies on two host seams —
`ctx.tools.guard()`
and `ctx.systemPrompt.section()` — and fails loud at mount if they change.
